messages:
incident-bot: 🔔 ALERT: GPU queue depth rising above 95% for customer 'acme-med' (private cluster eu-west-1). Autoscaler entering backoff. Paging oncall.
ryan: i'm on it, seeing sustained enqueue > 600 reqs/min, pod Pending -> ContainerCreating for ~8m.
maya: looks like the pool is depleted and the autoscaler failed to create new nodes — errors show repeated CNI timeout during cloud-init.
ryan: customer is on a private VPC with constrained IP range. autoscaler tried to spin 6 nodes, but only 1 succeeded. others timed out provisioning.
jules: any customer impact reports from CS? cs-rep-ana: they're seeing higher latency and 429s for real-time inference from some customer sessions. acme-med reported degraded response times ~5m ago.
sofia: fairshare metering shows one team within acme is sending long-generations and monopolizing GPU slots. combined with sticky warm nodes it's exhausting capacity.
ryan: ok immediate plan: 1) engage fallback routing to dedicated pool for non-sensitive traffic, 2) temporarily throttle long-gen requests via token bucket, 3) attempt manual node creation with simplified userdata.
maya: +1. Can we do a canary reroute for acme exactly? We should avoid sending PII to hosted. cs-rep-ana: confirmed we can route non-PII test traffic. acme consented to temporary routing for non-PHI workloads.
jules: i'm going to create a short-lived routing policy to move 30% of their traffic to dedicated-reserve-eu. command I will run:
```
redwoodctl routes update --customer acme-med --policy canary --target dedicated-reserve-eu --weight 30
```
sofia: i'm patching the autoscaler to relax the exponential backoff to allow one retry immediately while we debug. will monitor.
ryan: attempting manual node create with minimal cloud-init to bypass CNI initialization race. kubectl snippet for onprem agent:
```
kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: v1
kind: Node
metadata:
  name: manual-provision-temp-01
  labels:
    redwood/boot: "temp"
EOF
```
maya: logs from provisioner show "ipam: no available addresses" for the subnet. that confirms IP exhaustion. customer VPC only has /28 in the node subnet.
cs-rep-ana: escalating to acme network team to request a temporary /27 for node pool. they replied: "we can allocate, but needs 30–45m operational window".
ryan: beyond waiting, we should free up IPs: suggest evicting idle warm nodes and reducing stickyWarm threshold from 30m -> 5m.
sofia: implementing eviction: `kubectl annotate nodes --selector=redwood/warm=true redwood/evict=true` then scale down warm pool.
jules: reroute applied, logs show 25% of requests moving to dedicated-reserve-eu. error rate on private cluster dropping slightly.
maya: provisioning retry succeeded for 1 node after freeing IPs, but autoscaler still won’t schedule the remaining pending pods — kubelet reports CNI attach timeout 120s.
ryan: manual workaround: create a replacement node with host-networking to avoid CNIs for now (temp). running:
```
redwoodctl node create --region eu-west-1 --gpu-type a100 --host-network true --tags temp-evac
```
sofia: patch applied to token buckets to slow long-gen requests: `rate-limit acme-med:long-gen 10r/min` — should free some slots for short requests.
cs-rep-ana: acme confirmed they see significant improvement for interactive customers, but batch pipelines still queue.
ryan: creating incident runbook entry and will hand off to night oncall in 45m. summary + next steps: 1) monitor dedicated fallback and adjust weights, 2) coordinate with customer network for subnet expansion, 3) further harden autoscaler backoff and add IP precheck, 4) implement quota-per-team in acme tenancy to prevent future monopolization.
maya: logging remediation steps into the incident board and adding a ticket to infra: "autoscaler: pre-allocate IPs before node creation".
jules: i'll follow up with a rollback plan for the host-network node and ensure host-network nodes are removed once normal capacity restores.
sofia: leaving notes for next oncall: watch for node leak and sticky-scale behavior; confirm warm pool scaling thresholds.
ryan: handing to night oncall @maya in 45m. tagging incident as P2 for now, customer impact partial (some 429s, elevated latency). will update after subnet expansion outcome.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: severity P2, duration 00:27:10, impacted customer acme-med (partial). paging handoff to maya scheduled at +45m. links: https://redwood.incidents/2765432100
cs-rep-ana: i've sent the customer an interim status update and support ticket link. they appreciated the quick reroute. :thumbsup:
